repository_purpose: Reference implementation for deterministic hook control, validator feedback loops, and subagent lifecycle enforcement around Claude Code.
findings: The repo treats UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, and SubagentStop as distinct control points with different block/continue semantics; that taxonomy should survive translation into parent contracts.
Validator hooks and exit-code behavior are the important reusable primitive, not the raw `.claude` directory layout.
The upstream design is harness-specific at runtime, so the parent should absorb the doctrine as adapter-neutral policy and lifecycle contracts instead of copying Claude configuration verbatim.

capability_rows.upstream_feature_name: deterministic hook lifecycle and validator control
capability_rows.validation_method: Validate prompt gating, tool-use blocking, post-tool validation feedback, and stop/subagent-stop continuation rules as explicit allow/block/ask decisions with fail-loud outcomes.
capability_rows.blocker_or_dependency: Requires an adapter that exposes pre-prompt, pre-tool, post-tool, and stop lifecycle hooks; the parent contract is core even when a runtime adapter is still pending.
source_refs: docs/NOTION-DOCS/Capability Registry Reboot — Tools, Skills, Hooks, b29ab5c1ac7a4534a94bbe0c288ff0b9.md

trigger_logic: Treat user-prompt submission and pre-tool execution as the two proactive policy gates.
Treat post-tool and stop hooks as fail-loud validators that can require continued work when the result is incomplete.
actor_logic: The production gatekeeper owns allow/block/ask decisions before risky peer traffic or commands leave an actor.
Validation roles remain separate from builder roles even when the upstream repo demonstrates both in one Claude-oriented tree.
validation_summary: Require decision objects with explicit reasons and remediation.
Require no silent success fallback when a validator or stop hook finds missing work.

overlaps: Observability repo shares the same hook event taxonomy and turns it into durable telemetry.
Pi-to-Pi packet needs these gates to keep peer prompts and prod boundaries fail-loud.
blockers: Concrete runtime implementation is adapter-dependent, but the doctrine itself is not blocked.
